title: Pantry Garden - Action Items & Summary
text:
Meeting Date: January 9, 2026




2025 Harvest: 2,722 lbs produced
Volunteer Hours: 800 hours
Garden Plots: 2 of 23 community plots at Anderson (only 2 doing soil improvement)
Garden Started: 2019
Budget: $500 from County + Food Pantry Group + Larger Donors (Fire Fly, Arbor Systems)








Set up wash station with stainless steel table
Document inventory of items
Install French weave fencing between 8’ tall posts
Get forklift extender to move shed





Create management plan for fruit trees (Dog Park)
Prune 30 fruit trees (timing critical)
Empty compost bins - 2nd Saturday of April (coordinate with Boy Scouts - 2 or possibly 3)





Attend seeding event - March 14 at Penny’s
Submit seed wishlist to Farm & Fleet (donates seeds)
Coordinate garlic donation from Keene Gardens for next fall
Source potato coffee bags from roasters (Madison Food Pantry Garden connection)





Empty compost bins with Boy Scouts - 2nd Saturday of April
Plan Arbor Day Education event - Last Thursday or Friday of April





Address weed control strategy (add to future agenda)
Implement better mulching system (consider old billboard material)
Continue soil improvement practices
Decide on fertilizer approach: Feather meal vs Bone meal vs UREA vs Cover Crops

Note: Fish emulsion is expensive (“Three Sisters and one fish”)






Schedule next meeting in early February
Write letter to local businesses requesting volunteers (“BADGER NEEDS ‘PANTRY’”)
Research self-fed garden companion planting techniques
Evaluate woolets effectiveness from last year





Follow up with Michael from Agricultural Institute KERUSA about ancient grain (new/ancient grain we could grow)
Coordinate with Madison Area Food Pantry Garden for free compost
Recruit volunteer groups through Parks Site





Create equipment dream list for Madison Area Food Pantry Garden
Organize cardboard inventory (we have lots)









Garden plots are managed by Rooted as part of Madison Area Food Pantry Gardens
23 community plots at Addison total; we manage 2 plots
Only 2 plots (ours) are doing soil improvement
SNAP benefits cutback will increase need in 2026
Successfully grew 2,722 lbs of produce in 2025




Seed Selection Philosophy: “High yield = low effort” - Agricultural Education focus
Pepper Varieties:

Rainbow peppers: not great performance
Jalapeno: good
Poblano: good

Planning Considerations:

Potato growing in coffee bags (2-week timeframe)
Garlic planting and coordination with Keeve Gardens
Weed and mulch management needs improvement




Financial:

County budget: $500
Additional funding from Food Pantry Group
Larger donors: FireFly, Arbor Systems

In-Kind Donations:

Farm & Fleet: Seeds
Madison Area Food Pantry Garden: Free compost, woolets (2025)
Keene Gardens: Garlic donation (donated in 2025)

Materials Available:

Large cardboard inventory
Potential for old billboard material for mulching







Michael - Agricultural Institute KERUSA (ancient grain expert)
Rooted - Garden management organization
Garman Community Farm - New connection (downtown Oregon)
Farm & Fleet - Seed donations
Keene Gardens - Garlic donations
Madison Area Food Pantry Gardens - Compost and supplies
Madison Food Pantry Garden - Coffee bags from roasters






Weed control strategy discussion
Equipment needs and wishlist review
Volunteer recruitment and coordination
Companion planting implementation
Woolets effectiveness evaluation
